concepts.title: Overview of the Indian Economy at Independence

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Overview of the Indian Economy at Independence' refers to.
questions.a: At the eve of independence India was an agrarian economy with a large share of workforce in agriculture, low industrial base, widespread poverty and low literacy, so development policy after 1947 had to rebuild agriculture, industry and social sectors together.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Overview of the Indian Economy at Independence'.
questions.a: The unit overview frames the questions of growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity that guided planning from 1947 to 1990.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Overview of the Indian Economy at Independence' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Sectoral Structure: Agriculture, Industry and Services

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sectoral Structure: Agriculture, Industry and Services' refers to.
questions.a: The economy divides into primary agriculture and allied activities, secondary industry and manufacturing, and tertiary services, and the movement of workers and output among these sectors measures structural change in development.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sectoral Structure: Agriculture, Industry and Services'.
questions.a: A falling share of agriculture in output with rising industry and services shares marks the structural transformation targeted by development policy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sectoral Structure: Agriculture, Industry and Services' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Planning Goals: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Planning Goals: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity' refers to.
questions.a: Development planning in India from 1951 onward pursued four interlinked goals: economic growth raising aggregate output, modernisation of technology and social outlook, self-reliance reducing dependence on imports and aid, and equity spreading growth benefits to weaker sections.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Planning Goals: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity'.
questions.a: These goals sometimes conflict in the short run, so plans had to balance rapid growth with distribution and self-reliance with openness.
